A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ScMoE research. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable across all 18 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v2, allowing reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original vision accuracies, language-model perplexities, training and inference timings, and architectural analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original vision and language experiments and reports additional shortcut-position and gate ablations, two-node timings, and offloading memory and latency measurements.

M1.justification: v2 adds a learned, input-dependent shared-expert gate (Appendix A.3) and a CPU-offloading inference procedure with asynchronous, determinate expert migration (Section 3.3). These substantially extend the model and execution procedure. The original intermediate-position shortcut, now called Pos-2, and adaptive expert-parallel scheduling are retained.

E1.justification: ImageNet-1K, OpenWebText, and WikiText-103 remain unchanged, but v2 adds memory-limited, CPU-offloaded autoregressive inference on a single A30 GPU as a distinct deployment scenario. The two-node ScMoE evaluation also extends the standard-MoE hardware profiling already present in v1 Figure 1.

E2.justification: The vision shared-expert comparator belongs to v1's Residual MoE family but is substantively modified with SE-Gate. Figure 10 adds GPU-only and blocking Offload comparisons against Offload-Async. DGMoE timing comparisons and the GPT3 DGMoE/DGMoE-2 rows disappear, although DGMoE remains in appendix vision and GPT2 quality comparisons. Pre-gated MoE is discussed, not experimentally benchmarked.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a single-A30 offloading evaluation comparing resident, blocking-transfer, and asynchronous-transfer execution using normalized peak GPU memory and MoE-block latency. It also adds ScMoE timing experiments across two nodes with 16 GPUs and 16 experts. The retained vision and language training budgets and most hyperparameters are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds shortcut-position comparisons (Table 1), shared-expert gate on/off ablations (Table 5), and blocking versus asynchronous offloading analysis (Figure 10). v1's constant-weight sweep and ScMoE-2 vision experiment are removed. The representation/gating plots and DGMoE-Share experiment are retained and reframed rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix A.6 newly states that vision comparisons keep random seeds consistent and efficiency results average multiple samples over different periods. Neither disclosure establishes an increase in runs. Sample counts, seed values, confidence intervals, and significance tests remain unspecified.

E6.justification: The main vision comparison changes from ungated ScMoE/Residual MoE accuracies of 78.98%/79.02% to gated ScMoE/shared-expert accuracies of 79.38%/79.53%; v2 Table 5 retains the ungated values. New results include position/gate ablations, two-node ScMoE latency of 6.8 ms, and offloading memory/latency measurements. Several DGMoE results disappear. Matched language perplexities remain unchanged, and the GPT3 timing-to-speedup conversion is reciprocal redisplay rather than a new performance gain.

T1.justification: The residual-gradient derivation and scheduling bounds are retained through relocation and renumbering. A limited formal addition is the input-dependent shared-expert definition in v2 Equation 20, replacing the ungated MLP contribution in that configuration. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add determinate expert offloading for memory-limited inference as an explicit contribution, including claims of up to 60% memory reduction and 75% migration-overhead reduction. v1's prominent DGMoE and modality-discrepancy contributions give way to a ScMoE-centered account. The central distributed-acceleration and model-quality claims remain.

C2.justification: v1's hypothesis that vision/language differences arise from expert-combination counts is removed. v2 emphasizes shared-expert gating and develops representation-similarity, distinct-expert, and complementary-information explanations for shortcut effectiveness (Section 4.4; Appendix A.3). Section 4.3 also explains why larger models retain more offloading overhead through memory-bound decoding.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the shared-expert gate as a linear layer and documents CPU/GPU module placement and the trigger for asynchronous migration. Appendix A.6 clarifies the 16-expert two-node configuration. Most framework, tokenizer, and training disclosures are retained, while the Swin hyperparameter table loses its parameter-count row.

R1.justification: The broad MoE-advancements survey is replaced by focused memory-limited inference positioning, expanding the earlier contrast with Pre-gated MoE and EdgeMoE into speculative versus determinate migration. New citations include SE-MoE, SiDA, DeepSeekMoE, and Qwen1.5-MoE. Earlier coverage including StableMoE, MegaBlocks, and SmartMoE is removed, materially changing research positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction, architectural explanation, results discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around ScMoE. Theory and DGMoE specifications move into the appendix, experimental details move to A.6, and results gain distinct distributed, offloading, and shortcut-analysis sections. Fixed-MLP terminology is replaced by shared-expert terminology.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout and extensively redraws and redistributes architectural diagrams. It adds offloading diagrams, memory/latency plots, and ablation tables; expands the overhead figure to three panels; and removes the comprehensive architecture overview. Retained representation plots are resized and their panel labels corrected.

improvement.justification: v2 replaces v1's speculative modality explanation with direct gate ablations, tests the chosen shortcut position, and adds two-node ScMoE measurements beyond v1's single-node comparisons. These address important gaps in architectural justification and validation of the acceleration claim. Offloading results also expose both memory savings and residual latency costs. Although secondary DGMoE and constant-weight studies are trimmed and timing variability remains unquantified, the supporting evidence and scientific explanation improve substantially.
